title: Civilian Mediator Luckson Jean Secures Release of Kenscoff Hostages, Raising Questions Over Police Response
detail: Reporting on August 30, 2026 detailed how Luckson Jean — a Kenscoff-based community leader who founded the nonprofit Fondation Frè Luckson Zòn Pa Fè Moun (FLZPFM) — personally entered gang-controlled territory on August 28 and negotiated the release of 13 hostages (six children, including three under age 2, a 7-year-old, and two teenage girls, plus seven women) seized in the August 23 Kenscoff church massacre. UNICEF and Haiti's Social Welfare Research Institute (IBERS) supported the negotiations; gang leader Johnson "Izo 2" André, who leads the 5 Segonn faction, reportedly told intermediaries he would trust only Jean to retrieve the children, and no ransom was paid. "I thank God that the mission was successful despite the great risks I took to help save the lives of these innocent children," Jean said. The episode intensified scrutiny of the National Police response: PNH Director Vladimir Paraison had already ordered an investigation into whether the force's failure to stop the massacre reflected complicity or negligence, and the fact that a civilian intermediary succeeded in retrieving hostages where the state had not renewed public questions over the government's capacity to protect Kenscoff residents. More than 40 hostages remained in gang custody as of the release.

media.caption: Luckson Jean, founder of Fondation Frè Luckson Zòn Pa Fè Moun, carries a girl as he exits gang-controlled Kenscoff after negotiating the hostages' release, August 28, 2026
